b1-unit-46.46.1 Four apologies:
Narrator: One.
Danny: I'm so sorry I'm late. My bus broke down, so I had to walk from the station.
Director: Oh, that's OK. Actually, your students are still arriving. But please call me next time.
Danny: Of course. It won't happen again, I promise.
Narrator: Two.
Bruno: I have to apologize. I ate the sandwich in the fridge last night. I thought it was mine.
Danny: My chicken sandwich? I was saving it for lunch!
Bruno: I know. I'm really sorry. I'll buy you lunch today. Anything you want.
Danny: Anything? OK, then I forgive you... but only because I'm hungry.
Narrator: Three.
Agent: Customer service, good morning. How can I help you?
Danny: Hi. I ordered a lamp ten days ago, and it still hasn't arrived. The website says "delivered", but it isn't here.
Agent: Let me check... I'm sorry to hear that, sir. It seems the driver left it at the wrong address. We sincerely apologize for the mistake.
Danny: I'm afraid that's not good enough. I paid for express delivery! I expect a refund.
Agent: I understand, sir. We'll send you a new lamp tomorrow, and you'll get a full refund for the delivery.
Danny: OK. Thank you.
Narrator: Four.
Waiter: Excuse me. Who ordered the fish?
Carol: That was me.
Waiter: I'm afraid we don't have any fish left. I'm sorry about that. It was my mistake.
Carol: Oh, it doesn't matter. In that case, I'll have the chicken, please.
Waiter: Of course. And I'll bring you a free dessert.
Ana: Thank you. We really appreciate that.
b1-unit-46.46.2 Repeat: apologies and promises:
Narrator: I'm so sorry I'm late.
Narrator: I apologize for the mistake.
Narrator: It won't happen again.
Narrator: I'll make it up to you.
Narrator: Don't worry about it.
Narrator: I'm afraid that's not good enough.
